europmc-pmc6647174: Alpha-synuclein is the protein that clumps into Lewy bodies - the hallmark of Parkinson's. This review dives into the protein's shape-shifting structure and what it teaches about disease: how misfolding spreads and which forms are most toxic. The structural view points to where future drugs might intervene.
europmc-pmc6683074: Metabolic syndrome - the dangerous bundle of belly fat, high sugar, and bad lipids - bows to exercise. Reviewing human studies, the authors show physical activity and fitness chip away at every component. The prescription is refreshingly simple: move more, and the syndrome retreats.
europmc-pmc6717374: Cancer genomes carry the fingerprints of the forces that mutated them - smoke, UV, faulty repair. SigProfilerMatrixGenerator is a tool for visualizing these mutational patterns: plotting the small mutations so researchers can read their causes. The software turns cryptic catalogs into interpretable pictures.
europmc-pmc6890474: RNA packs hitch rides on the cell's recycling bins. This study found RNA clumps ride lysosomes for long hauls, using annexin A11 as a tether. The neuronal delivery system is neatly simple. On-site protein synthesis, delivered on time.
europmc-pmc6914774: Lung cancer care went gene-level - the map keeps growing. This review maps the new care terrain of aimed care in non-small-cell lung cancer. The personal care guide. Match the typo, pick the drug. The picks grow as labs win.
europmc-pmc6947974: Patient growths grown in mice - and in dishes - guide personal care. This review tours patient-derived mouse-grown growth models and mini-tumors: the live doubles of cancer. The tailored proving grounds. Med weak spots tried on your tumor twin. Bench-to-bedside lab most true stand-ins.
europmc-pmc6957674: Clinic apps promise much - the ward value is foggy. This review asks what is the ward value of mHealth for users: sorting apps by job. The evidence-based app guide. Stopping-early habits change to app cures. Rules trail behind installs.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-74: Who watches the toxic waste that leaves Army, Navy, and Air Force bases? The report spells out each player's part — and where the hand-offs could let poison slip through the cracks.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1174: The green-card lottery was leaking in 2007 — scammers and fake applicants gaming the Diversity Visa draw. GAO's report shows how fraud hobbled the State Department's grip on the popular program. The findings press for tougher screens on a beloved lottery whose cheaters threatened to kill it.
gao-gaoreports-b-299674: International Garment Processors tripled down in July 2007 — three case numbers, one apparel-contract fight — and GAO's combined ruling settles all three. The firm challenged the awards; the call works each claim. Stitched-together protests get a single, sewn-up answer.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-874: The Coast Guard's dream fleet was taking on water in 2007 — GAO's report says the Deepwater program's ships and planes faced deployment and management storms. The findings track the troubled modernization. The report warns that the guardians of the coast needed rescuing themselves.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-774: Troops voting from afar faced tech troubles in 2007 — GAO's report says electronic absentee voting needed real action plans to work. The findings map the obstacles between the soldier and the ballot box. The report's cause: the ballot should follow the soldier, with the glitches fixed first.
gao-gaoreports-b-308774: The Capitol's architect owed the compliance office money in this March 2007 GAO ruling, which settles who reimburses the investigation and monitoring costs. The call reads the fiscal law against the bill. The ruling decides which Capitol purse pays for the watchdog's work.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-74: The anti-piracy strategy needed an overhaul in 2007, and GAO's report says the STOP program required changes for long-term success. The findings prescribe the fixes. The report warns that the fake-goods fight needed more than slogans. The strategy had to stop the fakes.
gao-gaoreports-gao-06-674: Data brokers were not required to protect everything in 2006, and GAO's report says key privacy laws did not require resellers to safeguard all sensitive data. The findings expose the hole. The report warns that the personal dossiers deserved locks. The laws had to catch up.
gao-gaoreports-gao-06-274: Marine and Army logistics were out of sync in 2006, and GAO's report says the lack of a synchronized approach affected timely production. The findings target the disconnect. The report warns that the two services' supply lines needed joining. The approach had to be synchronized.
gao-gaoreports-b-297374: Remington Arms doubled its January 2006 protest — two case numbers, one arms fight — and GAO's combined ruling settles both. The firm challenged the awards, and the call weighs each claim. Paired filings get one careful answer. Two dockets, one fair verdict.
gao-gaoreports-gao-05-874: Federal student loan subsidy costs were hard to estimate in 2005, and GAO's report says challenges existed in projecting the costs. The findings map the difficulty. The report warns that the borrowers' subsidies deserved honest math. The challenges had to be faced.
openalex-w7206181474: Teenagers live on their phones, and this paper asks what that does to their reading and focus. The authors study how phones and apps have changed the way teens find facts, talk to each other, and learn. openalex-w7205000174: Feelings run every classroom, and teachers ignore them at their peril. This article brings together social-skills theory and brain science to explain how emotions shape daily school life: friendships, self-control, and learning itself. openalex-w7204533874: Wounds that will not heal need better options. This integrative review looks at platelet-rich plasma, or PRP, a treatment made from the patient's own blood, as a drug-free aid for healing injuries. openalex-w7204469274: Forcing vulnerable people into psychiatric lockup raises hard questions. arxiv-2606-16074: Patient boards and polls hold gold: how cures truly feel. But pulling clean facts from that chatter is hard. PVminerLLM2 does it better by learning which write-ups humans rate best, then copying that taste. It is for med-data folk who mine what patients say.
arxiv-2606-16174: Waves that spread out over time — light, water, quantum particles — obey "dispersive" equations, and mathematicians want sharp estimates of how they behave. This paper proves decoupling and discrete Strichartz estimates for such equations on the torus (a donut-shaped space). It is a pure analysis result aimed at specialists in partial differential equations and harmonic analysis.
arxiv-2606-16574: The "dark sector" — dark matter and dark energy — might interact with itself in ways we haven't probed. This cosmology paper studies intrinsic entropy couplings between dark-sector components: how disorder flows within the dark side of the universe. It targets cosmologists modeling the invisible majority of the cosmos.
arxiv-2606-16674: A companion study to the hyperbolic-photon-mode paper: what happens to a metal sitting near such exotic light modes? The authors work out the effects on the metal's properties when it's proximately coupled to hyperbolic photons. It targets condensed-matter theorists exploring how light environments reshape materials.
